text:
The evidence can't tell you whether the clearing was illegal. It doesn't cover legality, authorization, cause or responsibility.

What it does show: Hansen/UMD mapped about 13.5 ha of tree-cover loss in 2025 on this 345.6 ha property (3.91% of the area). The JRC 2020 map agrees that 98% of that area was forest in 2020. The MGAP 2021 forest map classifies about 13.1 ha as native forest and 0.4 ha as outside mapped forest, with no planted forest.

Important caveats:
- The finding is still pending corroboration. 2025 is the latest year in the series, so no later year confirms the loss is persistent.
- Hansen loss includes any stand replacement, so it doesn't by itself prove deforestation or land-use change.
- Nothing here identifies the cause (clearing, fire, storm, harvest) or who is responsible.

To assess legality, you would need to check Uruguayan authorization records (e.g., MGAP forest authorizations), the cause of the loss, and later imagery to confirm persistence.
